plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A hybrid flowering cherry that produces masses of delicate, almond-scented blossoms on bare branches before the leaves emerge. It is the iconic tree of spring hanami festivals and lines parks, rivers, and temple grounds.
plants.location: Japan, Washington D.C. (USA), South Korea, and temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: Nearly all Yoshino cherries are clones propagated by grafting, so trees in a region often bloom at almost exactly the same time.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A hardy bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers surrounded by paler yellow petals. It grows in woodlands and meadows and is the ancestor of many garden daffodil cultivars.
plants.location: Western Europe, including the UK, France, and Spain; naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: All parts of the daffodil contain lycorine and other alkaloids, making it toxic to most grazing animals, and galantamine from related Narcissus species is used in Alzheimer's medication.

plants.name: Cercis canadensis
plants.description: A small deciduous tree whose clusters of pea-like magenta-pink flowers burst directly from branches and even the trunk before heart-shaped leaves appear. It is common in woodland edges and widely planted in gardens.
plants.location: Eastern and central United States and northeastern Mexico
plants.funFact: Redbud flowers are edible and have a mildly tart flavor, and this tree displays cauliflory, meaning flowers grow straight from woody stems.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: Not usually in bloom now in the north, but its southern relatives are: in the Southern Hemisphere autumn, Amaryllis belladonna sends up leafless stalks topped with fragrant, trumpet-shaped pink blooms. This species thrives in Mediterranean-type climates.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (Southern Hemisphere: March to April)
plants.location: Western Cape, South Africa; naturalized in Australia, California, and parts of South America
plants.funFact: Known as the 'naked lady' because its flowers appear on bare stalks after the foliage has died back.
